title: Eliminating an oracle from a decider
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state deterministic oracle Turing machine over Boolean strings, let $D$ be a finite-state deterministic Turing machine over Boolean strings, and let $O,L$ be languages of Boolean words. Suppose $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is monotone, $M$ decides $L$ with oracle $O$ within $T(n)$ steps, and $D$ decides $O$ within $\tau(n)$ steps. Then there are a finite-state deterministic Turing machine $P$ and a natural number $a$ such that $P$ decides $L$ within $a(T(n)+1)(T(n)+1+\tau(T(n)))$ steps.
